22 A source of sound waves is moving at a constant speed directly towards a stationary observer.
The sound waves have a speed of 340 m s–1 and a frequency of 480 Hz. The observer hears
sound waves of frequency 650 Hz.
What is the speed of the source?
A
89 m s–1
B
120 m s–1
C
250 m s–1
D
340 m s–1

hints: Notice the source at $480 \text{ Hz}$ moves directly towards the stationary observer who hears $650 \text{ Hz}$, so the observed wavelength is shortened.
For an approaching source, use $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ with wave speed $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Rearrange to $v - v_s = v(f_s/f_o)$ and then find $v_s = v(1 - 480/650)$ before calculating in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the Doppler situation: source frequency $f_s = 480 \text{ Hz}$, wave speed $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, observed frequency $f_o = 650 \text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s$ towards stationary observer.
State the rule for a source approaching a stationary observer: wavefronts are crowded together so $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ and $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$.
Rearrange for the source speed: $v - v_s = v f_s/f_o$, so $v_s = v - v f_s/f_o = v(1 - f_s/f_o)$.
Substitute values with units: $v_s = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1} \times (1 - 480/650) = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1} \times 170/650$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $170/650 \approx 0.2615$, so $v_s \approx 340 \times 0.2615 \approx 88.9 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, about $89 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with correct units.

A.explanation: Gives $v_s \approx 89 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ from the approaching-source Doppler equation, matching the observed rise from $480 \text{ Hz}$ to $650 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Too large because it does not satisfy $650 = 480 \times 340/(340-v_s)$; it would give an observed frequency near $740 \text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Incorrectly uses the wavelength shift or frequency ratio the wrong way round, giving a source speed close to the wave speed.

D.explanation: Impossible for a normal Doppler shift since $v_s = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ would make the denominator zero and the observed frequency tend to infinity.
